title: Long-term outcomes of viscocanalostomy and phaco-viscocanalostomy in patients with narrow angle glaucoma

license.statement: Publisher licence (copyright under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany); made available via the PMC Open Access Subset for research re-use for the duration of the WHO COVID-19 pandemic declaration - not CC BY, record kept private

indication: narrow-angle glaucoma: mostly chronic narrow-angle glaucoma, also acute angle closure, ocular hypertension or normal tension glaucoma with narrow angles and nanophthalmos; most eyes had a prior laser peripheral iridotomy (prospectively maintained database, single surgical team, minimum 12 months follow-up; 70 eyes of 46 patients)

groups.description: un-augmented viscocanalostomy (no antimetabolite) with trabeculo-Descemet window, alone or combined with phacoemulsification (phaco-viscocanalostomy in about two thirds of eyes); intentional peripheral iridectomy when peripheral anterior synechiae blocked the window; Nd:YAG goniopuncture as postoperative intervention

series.notes: mean ± SD (caption: mean IOP); per-visit patient/eye numbers in the Table 2 header (fewer at later years: ordinary attrition; one patient missed year 1 and returned at year 2)

exclusions.what: Table 5 per-eye rows of the four failed eyes (pre-op IOP, IOP at failure, IOP at final follow-up)
exclusions.reason: eyes selected by a postoperative outcome (failure); final follow-up untimed
success proportions and Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Abstract/Results percent IOP reductions per year
exclusions.reason: derived summaries; the tabulated absolute means are used
the article reports a subgroup comparison only as a Kaplan-Meier p-value; no subgroup IOP is tabulated, so the whole cohort is extracted

notes: Context: viscocanalostomy alone or combined with phacoemulsification is recorded as nonpenetrating; the cohort mixes both variants and they are not tabulated separately.
Role: single cohort of the centre's standard un-augmented procedure, no experimental arm, so recorded as control.
Reference kind: patients used glaucoma drops before surgery (Table 1 R6, Table 2 R3) and no washout is described.
Method: the article does not name a tonometer.

Analysis set: 15 eyes without 12 months of data were excluded before analysis (selection by follow-up length, not by an outcome). Three eyes had further glaucoma surgery during follow-up; the article does not state that they were removed from later visit means.
Some patients contributed both eyes (70 eyes, 46 patients).
Mean number of drops per year is tabulated in Table 2 R3 (not extracted).
